title: What to learn from Buffett's Early Investments, Brett Gardner?
description:
📖 Get the book: Buffett's Early Investments by Brett Gardner (affiliate link): https://www.amazon.com/dp/1804090573?tag=goodinvesting-20

How did Warren Buffett earn his best returns in the 1950s and 1960s? Brett Gardner spent years in the original company documents to find out. In this talk he walks you through the cases in Buffett's Early Investments that matter most. He also shares what it takes to write and sell an investing book.

In this episode:
• The book covers 10 Buffett investments from the 1950s and 1960s, based on source documents that are hard to find.
• The first three cases were very cheap stocks that did poorly because of weak capital allocation.
• Philadelphia and Reading: a dying coal company became a conglomerate, and the stock went from about $9 to over $200.
• The hidden governance risk in Buffett's Disney investment: Walt Disney's personal holding company.
• American Express was the most profitable partnership investment. Brett explains the salad oil scandal.
